data.description:
# Voice-to-text pi extension using faster-whisper (Ctrl+Space)

## Problem statement

Pi has no voice input, so operators must type long prompts by hand. We need a pi
extension that captures microphone audio, transcribes it locally with
[faster-whisper](https://github.com/SYSTRAN/faster-whisper), streams the text
into the pi editor, and submits it automatically — toggled with a single
shortcut key.

## Users

Primary user: pi operators running the TUI on Linux/WSL2 with a CUDA GPU (the
requesting operator has an RTX 3050, 4 GB VRAM). Secondary user: any pi operator
who wants hands-free prompt entry.

Example user stories:

- As a pi operator, I press **Ctrl+Space**, speak my prompt, and it appears in
  the editor live, so I can dictate instead of typing.
- As a pi operator, when I stop speaking for a moment or press **Ctrl+Space**
  again, the prompt is sent exactly as if I had typed it and pressed Enter, so I
  don't have to touch the keyboard to submit.
- As a privacy-conscious operator, transcription runs entirely on my own
  machine (local GPU), so my audio never leaves my system.
- As an operator without CUDA, I can fall back to CPU inference by changing one
  setting.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. In the pi TUI, pressing **Ctrl+Space** (configurable keybinding) starts
   microphone capture; the footer/status area shows a clear recording indicator.
2. While recording, partial transcription results are streamed into the pi
   editor and each new partial replaces the previous one; on completion the
   editor contains the final transcript.
3. Recording stops and the transcript is **submitted automatically** when
   either (a) Ctrl+Space is pressed again, or (b) the user has been silent for
   more than 3 seconds (configurable). Submission behaves the same as if the
   operator had typed the text and pressed Enter (a normal user message,
   respecting pi's busy/steering mode).
4. Transcription is performed locally by faster-whisper on the CUDA GPU
   (`float16`) through a persistent Python worker that loads the model once per
   session; model size, device and compute type are configurable
   (default: `small` + `cuda` + `float16`, with automatic CPU `int8` fallback
   when CUDA is unavailable).
5. Audio is captured as 16 kHz mono 16-bit PCM through a configurable capture
   command (default works under WSLg/PulseAudio); if a required dependency is
   missing the extension shows an actionable notification and never crashes the
   pi session.
6. Unit tests cover the recording state machine, silence/pause detection,
   partial-transcript replacement, the Ctrl+Space toggle, and the worker
   protocol — without requiring a real microphone or GPU (capture and
   transcription are mocked).
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **TypeScript extension**, consistent with `pi-client/proxy-sse-signals`
  (jiti-loaded, no build step). Must use only the public `ExtensionAPI`.
- **Python bridge**: faster-whisper is Python-only, so the extension spawns a
  long-lived Python worker and talks to it over a line-delimited JSON protocol
  (model loaded once, not per utterance).
- **Platform**: Linux/WSL2 with CUDA. GPU target is an RTX 3050 with 4 GB VRAM —
  the default model must fit comfortably (`small`); `large-v3` may OOM and is
  not the default.
- **Local-only**: no cloud/network STT; privacy is a hard requirement.
- **Keybinding conflict risk**: Ctrl+Space is commonly intercepted by terminals
  and Windows IMEs, so the keybinding must be configurable and documented, with
  a recommended alternative.
- **WSL audio caveat**: WSL2 audio input requires WSLg/PulseAudio (or an
  ALSA→Pulse bridge). Capture backend must be selectable/overridable rather
  than hard-coded.

## Existing state

- Pi extension infrastructure already exists in this repo: `pi-client/` holds
  pi client extensions (`proxy-sse-signals`, `proxy-compaction-bridge`), each
  symlinked into `~/.pi/agent/extensions/` and unit-tested under `tests/unit/`
  with `node:test` (see `tests/unit/test-proxy-sse-signals.mjs`).
- The required pi APIs are available: `pi.registerShortcut(Key.ctrl("space"), …)`,
  `ctx.ui.setEditorText()/getEditorText()`, `ctx.ui.setStatus()`,
  `ctx.ui.notify()`, and `pi.sendUserMessage()`.
- Related precedent: the **speak** skill (`SA-0MRHSXIT00089DQ3`) is the inverse
  (text-to-speech) direction and uses a similar external-process bridge.
- faster-whisper is **not** installed in this environment. `arecord` exists but
  the current environment reports *no soundcards*; `ffmpeg`, `sox`, `parecord`
  and `pactl` are absent.
- No existing voice-input/STT work item or code (searched worklog and repo).

## Desired change

Add a new pi extension `pi-client/voice-input/` that:

1. Registers a configurable shortcut (default `Ctrl+Space`) that toggles
   recording.
2. Spawns a capture process (configurable; WSLg/PulseAudio-friendly default)
   producing 16 kHz mono PCM, and frames it for both transcription and
   energy-based silence detection.
3. Runs a persistent `faster-whisper` Python worker on the GPU, feeding
   accumulated audio to produce live partial transcripts.
4. Updates the pi editor live, shows a recording status indicator, and submits
   the final transcript (or leaves an error notification) when the stop trigger
   fires.
5. Ships a dependency/doctor check (faster-whisper import, CUDA availability,
   capture backend, model presence) that emits actionable guidance.
6. Includes docs (`docs/dev/voice-input.md`, extension `README.md`) and unit
   tests (`tests/unit/test-voice-input.mjs`), and is installable by symlink into
   `~/.pi/agent/extensions/`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `pi-client/voice-input/index.ts` — ExtensionAPI entry: shortcut registration, recording state machine, editor updates, auto-send, status/notifications.
- `pi-client/voice-input/recorder.ts` — spawns the capture command, frames 16 kHz PCM, computes per-frame RMS, drives silence/pause detection.
- `pi-client/voice-input/whisper-client.ts` — persistent worker lifecycle and line-delimited JSON protocol (start/feed/finalise/stop).
- `pi-client/voice-input/whisper_worker.py` — loads faster-whisper once (device/compute type from config) and transcribes incoming PCM chunks.
- `pi-client/voice-input/config.ts` — resolves settings/env (keybinding, model, device, compute type, silence threshold/ms, capture command).
- `pi-client/voice-input/doctor.ts` — preflight dependency/CUDA/backend/model checks with actionable messages.
- `pi-client/voice-input/README.md` — install, WSL/CUDA prerequisites, usage, troubleshooting.
- `docs/dev/voice-input.md` — design, protocol, configuration reference.
- `tests/unit/test-voice-input.mjs` — unit tests for the state machine, silence detection, partial replacement, toggle, and protocol.
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` — (optional) symlink the new extension into `~/.pi/agent/extensions/`.

## Related work

- `SA-0MRHSXIT00089DQ3` — Create a speak skill for text-to-speech (TTS) audio generation and playback (inverse direction; precedent for an external-process audio bridge).
- `SA-0MTWOYFLU004LB2R` — Add TTS to the standup skill (related audio tooling).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MLQ904LV1D1V8ZW** – Unit Tests and Manual E2E Script (completed)
- **SA-0MPKYR7SS000CO2J** – Ralph status command produces inconsistent reports (completed)
- **SA-0MKYE40VG1V2DTOX** – Agent error: 'wl show --thread' missing when running /impplement (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: again, auto, captures, com, create (+11 more)
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — matched: again, auto, com, create, extension (+8 more)
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_core.py` — matched: auto, com, create, editor, extension (+8 more)

> Note: the automated matches above are keyword-frequency noise (audit tooling,
> unrelated Ralph/status items); the manually curated entries are the
> genuinely related work.

## Risks and assumptions

- **VRAM limit (4 GB)** — `large-v3` may OOM; default `small` and document
  model trade-offs. *Mitigation*: automatic CPU `int8` fallback + clear errors.
- **WSL audio fragility** — capture may fail without WSLg/PulseAudio. *Mitigation*:
  configurable capture command + doctor check + actionable notification.
- **Ctrl+Space interception** — terminal/IME may swallow the key. *Mitigation*:
  configurable keybinding, documented alternative, `/voice-input` command fallback.
- **Partial-transcription latency** — naive re-transcription of a growing buffer
  can be slow. *Mitigation*: bounded sliding window / periodic cadence; tune in
  implementation.
- **Assumption**: "same as if I typed it" means the transcript is submitted as a
  normal user message via `pi.sendUserMessage()`, honouring pi's current
  steering/follow-up mode when busy.
- **Assumption**: live partial text is desired (the operator compared behaviour
  to typing), so partials update the editor while speaking.
- **Scope-creep risk**: multi-language selection, speaker diarisation,
  wake-word activation and cloud STT are explicitly out of scope; capture them
  as separate work items if raised.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Which faster-whisper model/hardware should be the default? — Answer
  (operator): "Yes I have a GPU CUDA to target". Research: `nvidia-smi` in this
  environment reports an NVIDIA RTX 3050 with 4 GB VRAM and CUDA 13.2 driver.
  Default chosen: `small` + `cuda` + `float16`, with CPU `int8` fallback.
  Source: interactive reply + `nvidia-smi`.

  **Answer (producer):** As answered- Q: Platform scope — Linux-only or cross-platform? — Answer (operator): "We can
  target Linux with WSL". Research: `arecord` present but no soundcard detected
  here; WSLg/PulseAudio is the expected capture path. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: When auto-send fires while pi is busy, should it steer, queue, or stay in
  the editor? — Answer (operator): "The behavior when sending should be the same
  as if I typed it in". Interpretation: submit as a normal user message and let
  pi's configured steering/follow-up mode apply. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: Should partial text stream live into the editor, or appear only on stop? —
  Answer (operator, implied by "same as if I typed it in"): live partial text.
  This is a documented assumption; revisit if undesired. Source: interactive
  reply (implicit).

## Post-audit recovery note (2026-09-27, audit run 2178s)

The automated `/skill:audit` run on 2026-09-26 failed for **infrastructure
reasons**, not because of any defect in the voice-input work:

- The local proxy was in `cheap` mode (`AUDIT_PARALLELISM=1`) while several
  audits ran concurrently; the Phase 1 parent screen fell back to `partial`
  because the audit concurrency queue saturated (no slot within 90s).
- The Phase 2 deep-analysis output could not be parsed (all 8 ACs marked
  `partial`) and the test-failure child's Phase 2 deep analysis timed out.
- The generated `Ready to close: No` verdict is therefore
  **fallback-tainted (not a genuine model assessment)** and the runner was
  required to restore the pre-audit state rather than demote.
- The runner's terminal lifecycle transition then failed with
  `Invalid status/stage combination: status "blocked" is not compatible with
  stage "in_review"`, leaving the item `blocked`/`in_review`. It has been
  recovered manually to `blocked`/`plan_complete`.

Side effects of the failed run (documented for the producer):

- The full project suite was **red** at the audited HEAD (4 commands, 11
  failures, all in the audit/test infrastructure); triage created 11 critical
  `test-failure` items and linked
  `SA-0MUIXZKH500624QM` as a blocking child/dependency of this item.
- The failed parent audit persisted short `Ready to close: No` child audits
  to the five voice-input children (because they carry no parseable AC
  heading), which reverted them from `completed`/`in_review` to
  `open`/`plan_complete` (two now `blocked`). Their implementation is
  complete and merged to `dev`.

This note intentionally changes the description hash so the stored
fallback-tainted audit becomes stale: **re-run the audit with `--force`**
(and preferably when the proxy is not saturated and the suite is green).

data.description:
Create the whisper worker protocol — persistent Python worker and TypeScript client.

**Files:**
- `pi-client/voice-input/whisper-client.ts` — TypeScript client
- `pi-client/voice-input/whisper_worker.py` — Python worker process

**whisper-client.ts responsibilities:**
- Spawn whisper_worker.py with configurable model/device/compute args
- Implement line-delimited JSON protocol (worker reads stdin, writes JSONL to stdout)
- Protocol messages: START (model init), FEED (PCM chunk), FINALISE (get transcript), STOP
- Handle partial transcripts: emit events as they arrive
- Handle errors: forward worker stderr/exit code as error events
- Lifecycle: init on recording start, feed PCM frames during recording, finalise on stop, clean exit

**whisper_worker.py responsibilities:**
- Import faster-whisper on startup
- Load model once (device + compute_type from config, with CPU int8 fallback)
- Run a loop: read JSON commands from stdin, write JSON responses to stdout
- FEED accumulates audio, transcribes at configurable cadence
- FINALISE returns the complete transcript
- Graceful shutdown on SIGTERM

**Unit tests (TDD — mock the Python worker process):**
- START message spawns worker and waits for READY response
- FEED messages buffer data and trigger partial transcript callbacks
- FINALISE collects all buffered data and returns final transcript
- STOP sends SHUTDOWN, waits for ACK, verifies clean exit
- Worker stderr/exit code produces error events, never crashes the client
